title: Customer communication and records
audience: Any owner, office contact or worker who communicates with customers and keeps customer records in a service business.
learningOutcomes: Communicate with the customer in writing and by phone so that each message is clear, timely and recorded.
Keep customer records that are accurate, current and held in the approved system.
Handle a change, complaint or query through the approved channel with a record of each step.

instruction.heading: Communicate clearly and on time
instruction.body: Confirm each booking in writing, with the date, time window, address, scope and any access arrangement. Send a reminder before the job, and tell the customer as soon as there is a change, such as a delay or a clash. Use plain language and avoid promises you cannot keep. When a customer asks a question you cannot answer, say you will check and confirm the answer in writing by a stated time. Keep the tone courteous even when the customer is frustrated.

instruction.heading: Keep accurate records
instruction.body: A customer record holds the contact details, the service history, the agreed scope, the access arrangements, the preferences and any special requirements. Update the record after each change, and date each update. Do not keep personal notes in unapproved places. Record only the information the business needs to deliver the service, and keep it secure. Where the customer asks to see or change their record, handle the request through the approved channel.

instruction.heading: Complaints and changes
instruction.body: A complaint or change request is recorded when it is received, with the facts, the customer's words and the date. Pass it to the designated contact, and tell the customer who will respond and when. Do not argue, blame another worker or agree to a refund or remedy without authority. Record the outcome and tell the customer the result in writing. Close the record only when the customer has been told the outcome.

procedure: Confirm each booking in writing with date, time window, address, scope and access.
Send a reminder before the job and tell the customer promptly of any change.
Update the customer record after each change, dated, in the approved system.
Record each complaint or change request with the facts and the customer's words.
Pass the complaint to the designated contact and tell the customer who will respond and when.
Record the outcome and tell the customer the result in writing before closing the record.

workedExamples.situation: A customer phones to say the cleaner did not turn up. You check the schedule and find the booking was moved by a colleague without telling the customer.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you say and record?
workedExamples.reasoning: Apologise for the missed visit, state the facts without blaming the colleague, and confirm a new time in writing. Record the complaint, the facts, the new booking and the designated contact who will review the cause. Do not offer a refund without authority.

equipmentAndPpe: Phone and email for customer communication

commonErrors.error: Making a verbal promise that is not recorded.
commonErrors.prevention: Confirm promises in writing and record them in the customer record.

commonErrors.error: Blaming a colleague in front of the customer.
commonErrors.prevention: State the facts, apologise, and pass the cause to the designated contact.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Customer records contain personal information. The Office of the Australian Information Commissioner states the Privacy Act applies to businesses above $3 million AUD annual turnover, and small businesses at or below that level are generally outside it.

qualityStandard: Each booking is confirmed in writing before the job.
Each customer record is dated and current.
Each complaint is recorded and closed only after the customer is told the outcome.
documentationEvidence: Booking confirmation, change notice and reminder records.
Complaint record with the facts, the response and the outcome notified to the customer.
summary: Confirm bookings and changes in writing and on time.
Keep customer records accurate, dated and in the approved system.
Record complaints, pass them on, and close them only when the customer knows the outcome.

knowledgeChecks.question: A customer asks a question you cannot answer. What should you do?
options: Guess the answer to keep them happy and avoid any delay in the call.
Guess an answer and move on to the next item on the list.
Say you will check and confirm the answer in writing by a stated time.

knowledgeChecks.question: A complaint is received by phone. What must you record?
options: The facts, the customer's words, the date and who it was passed to.
Nothing, unless it is written and the caller can be called back later.
Only the customer's name, the phone number and the time.

knowledgeChecks.question: What must each booking confirmation in writing include?
options: The date, the time window, the address, the scope and any access arrangement

officialReferences.title: Small business (Office of the Australian Information Commissioner)
officialReferences.covers: Read via summary fetch. The page states most small businesses are not covered by the Privacy Act, with the threshold given as annual turnover of $3 million or less. Exceptions apply regardless of turnover, including health service providers, businesses trading in personal information, credit reporting bodies, related businesses and businesses that have opted in. The page does not name the currency of the threshold. It recommends protecting personal information as good practice. Whether the Act applies to a particular business is not confirmed by this entry and should be checked with the OAIC.
